title: Mother before Queen
hookLine: the hymn of a thousand names opens by calling the goddess Mother, before Queen or throne
carry: the goddess is mother before she is queen
tomorrow: the gods have run out of answers. then, a fire.

lines: MOM AT SEVEN. DOCTOR BY NINE.
cards: At seven in the morning she's Mom, hunting for a missing shoe. By nine she's Doctor, signing charts. At lunch a friend calls her by a nickname from college.
At the temple an old aunty calls her beta, child. Same woman. Every name catches a different side of her, and nobody who loves her would pick just one.
Now make that vast. The Lalita Sahasranama is a hymn made almost entirely of names for the goddess, one after another, line after line. Today, how it opens.

teach.b: Sahasranama means a thousand names, and Lalita is the goddess they belong to. Tradition places the hymn in the Brahmanda Purana, as a teaching the god Hayagriva gives to the sage Agastya.
Some who worship her recite it name by name, at home or in temples. A hymn of names works differently from a story. There's no plot.
Each name is a small window, and you look through one, then the next. Over the coming days the path will open a few of those windows, not all of them. So, the first three names, in paraphrase.

teach.h: GREAT QUEEN, ON THE LION THRONE.
teach.b: Sri Maharajni: the great Queen. Srimat Simhasaneshvari: she who rules from the glorious lion throne. Notice the order.
Mother first, before the crown, before the throne, before any of her power is named.
Some teachers say that's the key to the whole hymn: whatever she is later, a warrior, a queen, the power behind the universe, she is that as a mother, and the one reciting comes to her as a child.
Then the throne and the lion: royal names. And the very first sound is Sri, the word the Sri Sukta days were built on. Here is the teaching under the order.
This is Shakta devotion, the worship of God as the Goddess, and its first move is to call the highest power Mother. You don't come to her as a subject with a petition.
That's why so many Hindus simply say Ma, at the temple, at the home shrine, under their breath in a hard week. Not a lesser name. The first one.

how: Some Hindus, especially in Shakta and Sri Vidya communities, recite the Lalita Sahasranama in full at home or in temples, sometimes offering a flower or a pinch of kumkum with each name.

games.q: the first names — tap the pairs.

s: the hymn tells one long story about the goddess
it's made of names, one after another, each a small window.
the very first name calls her Mother
Sri Mata, before Queen and before the lion throne.
in Shakta devotion, you come to the goddess first as her subject
the hymn opens with Mother: devotees come to her as her children first.

games.q: you're opening a hymn of names for the goddess who rules the universe. which name do you put first?
games.why: the Lalita Sahasranama opens Sri Mata, the auspicious Mother; Queen and the lion throne come next.

practice: Try what devotees do with this hymn: say the first three names slowly, Sri Mata, Sri Maharajni, Srimat Simhasaneshvari, with folded hands, or a flower or a pinch of kumkum for each if you have a shrine.
Then say only the first one a few more times, and rest there. If you don't pray, say the meanings in English, Mother, great Queen, the one on the lion throne, and notice which one feels closest.

wordCard.voice: The Lalita Sahasranama. A hymn of names for the goddess Lalita, which opens Sri Mata, the Mother, before Queen or throne.

orig.note: Sanskrit: śrīmātā, 'the auspicious Mother,' the first name in the Lalita Sahasranama.
